front: $R_f$ equals the distance traveled by the {{c1::spot}} divided by the distance traveled by the {{c2::solvent front}}, always between 0 and 1.
why: Rf definition is the standard TLC discrete

front: A carboxylic acid streaks badly on a silica TLC plate. What causes it and what fixes it?
why: Streaking fix is bench procedure, not tested

front: A protein with pI 5.0 is loaded in pH 7.0 buffer. Which ion exchanger binds it, and how do you elute it?
why: Ion exchanger choice from pI vs pH is asked nearly every exam

front: Acid-base extraction works because the {{c1::charged}} form of a compound is water soluble while the {{c2::neutral}} form prefers the organic layer.
why: Charged-in-water, neutral-in-organic is the whole basis of extraction questions

front: Affinity chromatography separates by {{c1::specific binding}} to an immobilized ligand, as when a His-tagged protein binds a {{c2::nickel}} column.
why: Affinity/His-tag columns appear in many protein-purification passages

front: After extraction the organic layer is dried over {{c1::anhydrous $MgSO_4$ or $Na_2SO_4$}}, then concentrated by {{c2::rotary evaporation}}.
why: Drying agent and rotovap are workup context a passage may mention

front: After the acid wash, {{c1::NaHCO3}} removes the carboxylic acid and then {{c2::NaOH}} removes the phenol, leaving the hydrocarbon behind.
why: Sequential bicarbonate then hydroxide wash is the classic extraction problem

front: All chromatography relies on differential partitioning between a {{c1::mobile}} phase and a {{c2::stationary}} phase.
why: Mobile vs stationary phase partitioning underlies every chromatography question

front: Ammonium sulfate precipitates proteins by {{c1::salting out}}, competing for the water that hydrates them.
why: Salting out shows up as passage context, rarely as the tested step

front: An ether solution holds benzoic acid, aniline, phenol, and naphthalene. What is the first wash, and what does it remove?
why: Four-component extraction application; first wash choice is a common item

front: An organic layer contains an amine and a neutral compound. How do you separate them?
why: Acid wash pulling amines into water is a staple extraction item

front: Choose GC when the analyte is {{c1::volatile and thermally stable}}; choose HPLC when it is {{c2::nonvolatile or heat sensitive}}.
why: GC vs HPLC choice is a second-tier method-selection question

front: Density-gradient (isopycnic) centrifugation separates particles by {{c1::buoyant density}}, each band settling where its density matches the medium.
why: Density-gradient centrifugation mainly appears via Meselson-Stahl context

front: Distinguish Southern, Northern, and Western blots.
why: Southern/Northern/Western blot targets are tested on nearly every exam

front: Gas chromatography separates volatile compounds primarily by what property?
why: GC by boiling point is a secondary method detail

front: How do you determine experimentally which layer in a separatory funnel is aqueous?
why: Water-drop layer test is bench procedure trivia

front: How does a sandwich ELISA generate a quantitative signal?
why: ELISA mechanism is common in immunology and assay passages

front: How does affinity chromatography work?
why: Restates the affinity chromatography card

front: How does an impurity affect a solid's melting point, and why is that diagnostic?
why: Melting-point depression as a purity check is a frequent discrete

front: How does ion-exchange chromatography separate proteins, and how are bound proteins released?
why: Ion exchange by charge and salt/pH elution is core protein purification

front: How does isoelectric focusing separate proteins?
why: Isoelectric focusing at pI with zero net charge is tested every year

front: In a separatory funnel, diethyl ether forms the {{c1::upper}} layer over water while dichloromethane forms the {{c2::lower}} layer.
why: Ether over water vs DCM under is a secondary density detail

front: In an assay, a {{c1::negative}} control contains everything except the variable of interest and should produce no signal.
why: Negative vs positive controls are tested on essentially every exam

front: In differential centrifugation, in what order do cellular components pellet as speed is increased?
why: Differential centrifugation order is second-tier cell fractionation detail

front: In DNA gel electrophoresis, why do all fragments migrate toward the anode regardless of sequence?
why: DNA size separation and migration toward the anode is core electrophoresis

front: In IR, a strong sharp band near {{c1::1700}} cm$^{-1}$ signals a C=O, while a broad band across 3200-3600 signals {{c2::O-H}}.
why: C=O at 1700 and broad O-H at 3200-3600 are the IR facts tested every year

front: In isoelectric focusing a protein migrates through a pH gradient until the pH equals its {{c1::pI}}, where its net charge is {{c2::zero}}.
why: Restates the isoelectric focusing card

front: In mass spectrometry the molecular ion peak gives the {{c1::molecular weight}}, and an M+2 peak nearly equal in height indicates {{c2::bromine}}.
why: Mass-spec isotope patterns are off-outline trivia for the MCAT

front: In reverse-phase HPLC, which compounds elute first and why?
why: Reverse-phase elution order is a common chromatography reasoning item

front: On a normal-phase silica TLC plate, how does a more polar compound behave?
why: Polar compounds low Rf on silica is the standard TLC question

front: Raising mobile-phase polarity on a normal-phase TLC plate {{c1::raises}} $R_f$, because the solvent competes for {{c2::the polar silica surface}}.
why: Effect of eluent polarity on Rf is a common TLC follow-up

front: Recrystallization exploits the fact that solubility {{c1::increases with temperature}}: dissolve in hot solvent, then cool slowly to grow pure crystals.
why: Recrystallization principle is standard purification content

front: SDS-PAGE separates proteins by {{c1::molecular mass}} alone, because SDS denatures them and coats them with {{c2::uniform negative}} charge.
why: SDS-PAGE separating by mass alone is tested every year

front: Size-exclusion (gel-filtration) chromatography elutes {{c1::large}} molecules first, because they cannot enter the pores of the beads.
why: Size exclusion large-first is a perennial discrete

front: Size-exclusion chromatography also serves to {{c1::desalt}} a protein, since small ions enter the beads and elute {{c2::last}}.
why: Desalting use of size exclusion is a secondary application

front: Southern blotting detects {{c1::DNA}}, Northern blotting detects {{c2::RNA}}, and Western blotting detects protein using antibodies.
why: Restates the blot card

front: State Beer's law.
why: Beer's law is the calculation equation for absorbance questions

front: To pull a carboxylic acid out of an ether layer while leaving a phenol behind, wash with {{c1::aqueous NaHCO$_3$}}.
why: Bicarbonate pulls the acid but not the phenol; tested every year

front: To recover an extracted amine as its free base, {{c1::basify}} the aqueous layer and then re-extract into fresh organic solvent.
why: Recovering the free amine is a second step after the extraction concept

front: Two-dimensional gel electrophoresis separates first by {{c1::pI, using isoelectric focusing}} and then by {{c2::mass, using SDS-PAGE}}.
why: 2D gel order (IEF then SDS-PAGE) is a common proteomics item

front: UV-Vis absorbance is most informative about what structural feature, and what law quantifies it?
why: Conjugation shifting UV absorbance and Beer's law appear regularly

front: Vacuum distillation lowers ambient pressure so a compound boils at a {{c1::lower}} temperature, protecting {{c2::heat-sensitive}} compounds from decomposing.
why: Vacuum distillation for heat-sensitive compounds is a frequent discrete

front: What does a standard curve accomplish in a quantitative assay, and what is its limitation?
why: Standard curve and linear range are secondary assay reasoning

front: What does gel electrophoresis separate by, and which way does DNA move?
why: Restates the DNA electrophoresis card

front: What does SDS-PAGE separate by?
why: Restates the SDS-PAGE card

front: What is an azeotrope and why does it limit distillation?
why: Azeotropes are a second-tier distillation limitation

front: What is the principle of size-exclusion chromatography?
why: Restates the size-exclusion card

front: What key reagent makes PCR possible?
why: Taq's heat stability is a common PCR item

front: What three pieces of information does a proton NMR spectrum provide?
why: Shift, integration, splitting are the NMR basics the outline names

front: When is fractional distillation required rather than simple distillation?
why: Fractional vs simple distillation threshold is the classic distillation discrete

front: Which purification method suits a solid product contaminated with a small amount of a similar impurity?
why: Method selection overlaps the recrystallization card

front: Which single property does each exploit: distillation, recrystallization, dialysis, electrophoresis?
why: Property exploited by each technique is exactly the interpretation the exam wants

front: Which technique separates enantiomers, and why do the usual methods fail?
why: Enantiomers needing a chiral environment is a classic separation item

front: Why are three small extractions more efficient than one large extraction using the same total solvent volume?
why: Multiple small extractions is secondary partition reasoning

front: Why choose NaHCO3 over NaOH to extract a carboxylic acid from a mixture that also contains an ester?
why: Ester saponification nuance on the bicarbonate choice

front: Why does a protein purification scheme run ion exchange before size exclusion?
why: Purification scheme ordering is procedural design detail

front: Why does washing with brine (saturated NaCl) help during an aqueous workup?
why: Brine wash is bench procedure trivia

front: Why is a co-spot lane run on a TLC plate?
why: Co-spot lanes are TLC procedure detail

front: Why is the sedimentation coefficient in Svedberg units not additive?
why: Non-additive Svedberg units is a known trap but secondary

front: Why must a spectrophotometer be blanked before a sample's absorbance is measured?
why: Blanking is supporting reasoning for absorbance questions
